in_hebrew.name: רָחַל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The Hebrew name Rahal is derived from the Hebrew word rachal, meaning 'eunuch' or 'emasculated'. This name is mentioned in the Hebrew Bible as the name of a Midianite princess who became the wife of the biblical patriarch Jacob. In this context, the name Rahal likely refers to her status as a eunuch or a woman who has been separated from her reproductive capabilities.

in_greek.name: Ραχαλ
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name Rachel is derived from the Hebrew name Rahal. In Greek, the name Rachel is transliterated as Ραχαλ. The Greek form of the name preserves the original Hebrew meaning of 'eunuch' or 'emasculated', as the name Rachel was borne by a biblical figure who was a princess of the Midianites and later became the wife of the patriarch Jacob. In the Greek language, the name Rachel came to be used as a feminine given name, and it has been a popular name in the Greek-speaking world throughout history.

in_latin.name: Rachelis
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Rachelis is derived from the Greek name Rachel. In Latin, the name Rachel is transliterated as Rachelis. The Latin form of the name preserves the original Greek and Hebrew meanings of 'eunuch' or 'emasculated', as the name Rachel was borne by a biblical figure who was a princess of the Midianites and later became the wife of the patriarch Jacob. In the Latin language, the name Rachelis was used as a feminine given name, and it has been a popular name in the Latin-speaking world throughout history.
